questions.prompt: Complete: Dün eve geç ___ (gelmek, ben).
questions.explanation: The definite past -DI combines with first-person singular -m: gel-di-m → geldim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dün kahve ___ (içmek, biz, negative).
questions.explanation: Past negation is verb stem + -mA + -DI + person: iç-me-di-k → içmedik.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past-tense form: “I was a student last year.” Geçen yıl ___ .
questions.explanation: A vowel-final noun takes buffer y before past copula: öğrenci + ydi + m → öğrenciydim.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question: “Were you at home yesterday?”
questions.explanation: A past nominal question places mi before the past personal ending: evde miydin?

questions.prompt: Complete: Çocukken her gün parkta ___ (oynamak, ben, past continuous).
questions.explanation: Past progressive is -(I)yor + -DI + person: oynuyordum.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben küçük___ İstanbul’da yaşıyordum. (When I was little.)
questions.explanation: The temporal suffix -(y)ken means “while/when”: küçükken.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct attached form meaning “by bus”.
questions.explanation: The instrumental/comitative ile can attach as -(y)lA: otobüsle.

questions.prompt: You are politely addressing a group. Complete: Lütfen içeri ___ (girmek).
questions.explanation: Polite/plural second-person command of girmek is girin.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative polite command: “Please do not smoke.”
questions.explanation: İçmeyin is the polite/plural negative command: iç- (drink/smoke) + -me- (negation) + -yin (polite imperative). The other options are indicative statements, not requests.

questions.prompt: Complete: Şeker___ çay istiyorum. (without sugar)
questions.explanation: The suffix -sIz means “without” and follows four-way vowel harmony: şeker + -siz → şekersiz (“sugar-free”). By contrast, şekerli means “with sugar.”

questions.prompt: Complete: Haydi birlikte ___ (gitmek, biz, suggestion).
questions.explanation: First-person plural suggestion uses -(y)AlIm: gid-e-lim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ankara, İstanbul’___ daha küçük.
questions.explanation: Comparisons use the ablative case -DAn before daha: İstanbul’dan daha küçük.

questions.prompt: Choose the superlative: “Ali is the tallest student in this class.” Bu sınıftaki ___ uzun öğrenci Ali.
questions.explanation: The superlative marker en precedes the adjective: en uzun.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu araba___ satın aldım. (I bought this car.)
questions.explanation: A definite direct object with demonstrative bu takes accusative -(y)I: bu arabayı.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct definite-object form of kitap (book): “I finished the book yesterday.”
questions.explanation: Kitabı is the definite accusative of kitap (p → b before -ı); bitirdim is first-person singular definite past. The other choices either omit accusative marking or change the tense.

questions.prompt: You are telling a friend you bought a book, but neither of you has a particular book in mind. Which sentence expresses this indefinite, nonspecific object?
questions.explanation: An indefinite direct object can appear without accusative: bir kitap aldım.

questions.prompt: Complete the modifier meaning “on the table”: Masa___ kitap benim. (“The book on the table is mine.”)
questions.explanation: The modifier masadaki (“on the table”) is formed with locative -da and attributive -ki: masa-da-ki. The other endings do not form the required attributive modifier.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct spelling for “I am coming too.”
questions.explanation: The additive particle de (“too”) is written separately: Ben de geliyorum.

questions.prompt: Yarın Ankara’ya ___ (gitmek, ben, future).
questions.explanation: Future -(y)AcAk takes first-person singular and stem alternation: gideceğim.

questions.prompt: Dün seni aramayı planlıyordum, ama zamanım olmadı. Niyetimi geçmişte gelecek zamanla ifade et: Seni ___ . (aramak, ben)
questions.explanation: Future-in-the-past -AcAktI expresses an unrealized intention: arayacaktım.

questions.prompt: ___ göre bu film çok güzel. (according to me)
questions.explanation: Göre (“according to”) requires a dative-marked pronoun. Ben changes to bana in the dative, so bana göre means “according to me / in my opinion”; beni is accusative.

questions.prompt: Sabah uyandın ve sokakların ıslak olduğunu gördün. Şaşırarak söyle: “Aa, yağmur ___!” (You infer it rained.)
questions.explanation: The inferred/reported past -mIş gives yağmış (“apparently it rained”). Seeing wet streets is evidence for an inference; yağıyor instead says it is raining now.

questions.prompt: Duyduğuma göre yarın ___ (gelmek, o, reported future).
questions.explanation: Gelecekmiş combines the future gelecek (“will come”) with reported-information -miş (“apparently / reportedly”). Geldi is simple past and does not convey reported future.

questions.prompt: Ali is not answering his phone, so you guess he is at home. Complete with the present-time third-person predicate ending -DIr: Ali şu anda evde___.
questions.explanation: Evde-dir contains the third-person predicate ending -DIr. In this context it can convey a supposition (“Ali is probably at home”), though -DIr can also be used for more formal assertions.

questions.prompt: Her sabah kahve ___ (içmek, ben, habitual aorist).
questions.explanation: İçerim is the first-person singular aorist: iç- + -er + -im. With her sabah (“every morning”), it expresses a repeated habit rather than one completed or planned event.

questions.prompt: Which form means “I can speak Turkish” (ability, not merely the fact that I speak it)? Türkçe ___ .
questions.explanation: Ability -(y)Abil- combines with aorist and person: konuşabilirim.

questions.prompt: Eskiden burada ___ (yaşamak, biz, habitual past).
questions.explanation: Yaşardık combines the aorist stem yaşar- with past -dı- and first-person plural -k. Eskiden (“in the past”) supports the meaning “we used to live.”

questions.prompt: Complete with the conjunction that explicitly gives the reason: Evde kaldım, ___ hastaydım. (I stayed home because I was sick.)
questions.explanation: Çünkü introduces a reason: I stayed home because I was sick.

questions.prompt: Türkçe öğren___ için her gün çalışıyorum.
questions.explanation: The infinitive -mAk is used before için: öğrenmek için.

questions.prompt: Kahvaltı yap___ sonra işe gidiyorum.
questions.explanation: The sequence -DIktAn sonra means “after doing.” Yap- + -tık- + -tan → yaptıktan, so kahvaltı yaptıktan sonra means “after having breakfast,” not “before.”

questions.prompt: Eve gid___ uyudum. (and then I slept)
questions.explanation: The converb -(y)Ip links successive actions: gidip uyudum.

questions.prompt: Complete using the manner converb -(y)ArAk: Otobüse bin___ şehir merkezine gittim. (I traveled to the city center by taking the bus.)
questions.explanation: Binerek is bin- (“board”) + -erek, a converb indicating manner or a means of travel: “by taking the bus.” Binmeden means “without boarding,” a different relationship.

questions.prompt: Yüz___ sağlıklıdır. (Swimming is healthy.)
questions.explanation: Yüzme turns the verb yüz- (“swim”) into an activity noun. Thus yüzme sağlıklıdır means “swimming is healthy”; the other endings make finite or future forms.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported instruction: Öğretmen öğrencilere sessiz ol___ söyledi. (The teacher told the students to be quiet.)
questions.explanation: Reported commands can use -mA with a possessive ending and accusative: olmalarını.

questions.prompt: Which word contains only back vowels?
questions.explanation: Kapı contains a and ı, both back vowels. Şehir and kedi contain front vowels e/i; güneş contains front vowels ü/e.

questions.prompt: Choose the plural of “ev”.
questions.explanation: The plural suffix follows two-way vowel harmony: evler.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben doktor ___ . (I am not a doctor.)
questions.explanation: First-person singular negation of a nominal predicate is değilim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sen öğrenci ___? (Are you a student?)
questions.explanation: The question particle agrees with the last vowel in öğrenci: misin.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz Türk___ . (We are Turkish.)
questions.explanation: The first-person plural nominal predicate ending is -üz after Türk.

questions.prompt: Complete with the neutral present-time existential form: Masada bir kitap ___. (There is a book on the table now.)
questions.explanation: Var states that something exists in the present. Vardı refers to past existence, varmış adds reported or inferred information, and yok means there is none.

questions.prompt: Choose the ordinal meaning “third”.
questions.explanation: Üçüncü is the ordinal “third”: üç (three) + the ordinal suffix -üncü. Üçte is a locative form, not an ordinal number.

questions.prompt: Complete: Şu anda Türkçe ___ . (I am studying Turkish.)
questions.explanation: Çalışıyorum combines çalış- with the present continuous -ıyor and first-person -um. Şu anda (“right now”) calls for an action in progress, not habitual, future, or past.

questions.prompt: Complete using the negative present continuous (-mIyor): Şu anda işe ___ . (I am not going to work right now.)
questions.explanation: Gitmiyorum is git- + negative -mi- + present continuous -yor + first-person -um. It describes not going now; gitmeyeceğim instead describes a future non-action.

questions.prompt: Complete the destination suffix (including any buffer consonant): Yarın Ankara’___ gidiyorum.
questions.explanation: Ankara ends in a vowel, so the dative ending -a needs buffer -y-: Ankara + -ya → Ankara’ya (“to Ankara”). -da marks location and -dan marks departure.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kitap raf___ duruyor. (The book is on the shelf.)
questions.explanation: Raf ends in voiceless f, so the locative suffix is -ta rather than -da: raf + -ta → rafta (“on the shelf”). -tan would mean “from the shelf.”

questions.prompt: Complete: Okul___ geliyorum. (I am coming from school.)
questions.explanation: The ablative -DAn expresses motion or origin “from”: okul + -dan → okuldan (“from school”). -da instead means “at school,” and -a means “to school.”

questions.prompt: Complete: Ders___ önce kahve içiyorum. (I drink coffee before class.)
questions.explanation: Dersten önce means “before class.” The noun ders takes ablative -ten after the voiceless s; önce follows that ablative form.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “It is quarter past three.”
questions.explanation: Saat üçü çeyrek geçiyor means “it is a quarter past three” (3:15). Çeyrek var expresses time remaining until an hour, while buçuk means half past.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ders saat üçü çeyrek ___ başlıyor. (Class starts at 3:15.)
questions.explanation: When giving the time of a scheduled event, Turkish uses the converb geçe: saat üçü çeyrek geçe = “at 3:15.” Geçiyor states the current clock time instead.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim araba___ . (This is my car.)
questions.explanation: Araba ends in a vowel, so first-person singular possession adds -m directly: araba + -m → arabam (“my car”). -sı marks third-person possession.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu onun araba___ . (This is his/her car.)
questions.explanation: Vowel-final araba takes buffer -s- before third-person possessive -ı.

questions.prompt: Supply the full genitive suffix after the apostrophe: Ali’___ kitabı burada. (Ali’s book is here.)
questions.explanation: Ali ends in a vowel, so the genitive takes buffer -n- plus front-vowel -in: Ali’nin kitabı (Ali’s book). The apostrophe separates the proper name and its case ending.

questions.prompt: Complete the noun compound: Türk kahve___ . (Turkish coffee.)
questions.explanation: An indefinite noun compound has the possessive ending on its head: Türk kahvesi.

questions.prompt: Choose the bare adjective + noun phrase for “a beautiful house,” with no possessive suffix.
questions.explanation: Attributive adjectives normally precede the noun: güzel ev.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question: “Did you go home yesterday?”
questions.explanation: The past marker -DI takes person agreement; the question particle is separate.

questions.prompt: Complete: “She went.” (gitmek, definite past)
questions.explanation: After the voiceless t in git-, the past suffix starts with t.

questions.prompt: Complete: “I was not a student.”
questions.explanation: Değil takes the past nominal-predicate ending -di and first-person -m.

questions.prompt: Complete: “I was not sleeping.”
questions.explanation: The negative past continuous uses -mIyor + -du + personal ending.

questions.prompt: Which means “Were you studying?”
questions.explanation: Past continuous question: -yor + question particle + past/person.

questions.prompt: Translate “I went with my friend.”
questions.explanation: The instrumental/comitative suffix -(y)lA expresses “with”.

questions.prompt: Give an informal singular command: “Come!”
questions.explanation: The informal singular imperative is the bare verb stem.

questions.prompt: Give a third-person singular command: “Let him/her come!”
questions.explanation: The third-person imperative uses -sIn: gel- + -sin → gelsin (“let him/her come”). Gel is a singular second-person command; gelin addresses a plural or polite second person.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “with sugar / sugary.”
questions.explanation: The adjective suffix -lI means “with / containing”: şeker + -li → şekerli (“sugary”). Its opposite, -sIz, gives şekersiz (“without sugar”).

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “without salt.”
questions.explanation: Tuzsuz means “without salt”: tuz (salt) + -suz, the back-vowel form of the privative suffix -sIz. Tuzlu means “salty,” the opposite.

questions.prompt: Complete: “Izmir is warmer than Ankara.” İzmir, ___ daha sıcak.
questions.explanation: Comparatives with daha use the ablative -DAn on the comparison point.

questions.prompt: Which means “the most beautiful city”?
questions.explanation: En before an adjective forms a superlative: en güzel şehir = “the most beautiful city.” Daha güzel means “more beautiful” and expresses comparison, not a superlative.

questions.prompt: Complete: “I saw the dog.” ___ gördüm.
questions.explanation: The definite object takes accusative -(y)I; köpek softens to köpeğ-.

questions.prompt: Translate “I also want tea.”
questions.explanation: The additive particle de (“also”) is written separately.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means simply “I am at home,” without adding “also/too”?
questions.explanation: The locative -de is attached to the noun, unlike additive de.

questions.prompt: Complete with the negative future suffix -(y)AcAk: Yarın ___ . (gitmek, ben; “I will not go tomorrow.”)
questions.explanation: Future negation uses -mA + -(y)AcAk with appropriate sound changes.

questions.prompt: Choose the question formed with the future-tense suffix -(y)AcAk: “Will you come tomorrow?”
questions.explanation: Future questions use the separate question particle after the future form.

questions.prompt: Choose the form meaning “in Turkish / Turkish-style” in “Türkçe konuşuyorum.”
questions.explanation: The equative -CA/-CE appears in language names such as Türkçe.

questions.prompt: Complete: “According to me, this is good.” ___ göre bu iyi.
questions.explanation: Göre (“according to”) requires a dative pronoun: ben → bana, so bana göre means “in my opinion.”

questions.prompt: Translate “like a child.”
questions.explanation: Gibi follows a noun to express similarity: çocuk gibi = “like a child.” Çocuk için means “for a child,” while çocuğa marks the dative “to a child.”

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently she did not come.”
questions.explanation: Gelmemiş is gel- + -me- (negative) + -miş (reported/inferred past): “apparently did not come.” Gelmedi instead asserts the simple definite past.

questions.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Did he apparently go?” (reported/inferred past).
questions.explanation: Gitmiş mi? combines the reported/inferred past gitmiş with the separate question particle mi. Gitti mi? asks about the definite past without that evidential nuance.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently he is a teacher.”
questions.explanation: Öğretmenmiş adds reported/inferred -miş directly to the noun predicate: “apparently (he/she) is a teacher.” Öğretmendi refers to being a teacher in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently she is sleeping.”
questions.explanation: Uyuyormuş combines present continuous uyuyor with reported/inferred -muş: “apparently she is sleeping.” Uyuyacakmış refers instead to a reported future event.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently he will not come.”
questions.explanation: Gelmeyecekmiş combines negative future gelmeyecek (“will not come”) with reported-information -miş: “apparently he will not come.” Gelmemiş is a reported past.

questions.prompt: Use the negative aorist (geniş zamanın olumsuzu): “I do not drink coffee.” Kahve ___ .
questions.explanation: İçmem is the first-person singular negative aorist, expressing a general habit: “I do not drink.” İçmiyorum is negative present continuous and can describe the current situation.

questions.prompt: Choose the question in the aorist (geniş zaman) meaning “Do you read books generally?”
questions.explanation: Okur musun? uses the aorist okur plus separate question particle mu and second-person ending -sun. It asks about reading generally, unlike okuyor musun? (“are you reading?”).

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence using the negative ability suffix -(y)AmA- to say “I cannot swim.”
questions.explanation: Yüzemem expresses inability using the negative ability construction: yüz- + -e-me- + -m. Yüzmüyorum means “I am not swimming,” which does not necessarily mean inability.

questions.prompt: Choose “I used to live here.”
questions.explanation: Eskiden (“formerly”) with yaşardım, the past aorist of yaşamak, conveys “I used to live here.” Yaşıyorum is present and yaşayacağım is future.

questions.prompt: Choose the connector meaning “therefore / for this reason.”
questions.explanation: Bu yüzden introduces a result; çünkü introduces a reason.

questions.prompt: Complete with -mAk üzere to express purpose: Seni görmek ___ geldim.
questions.explanation: The pattern verb + -mAk üzere can express purpose: seni görmek üzere geldim = “I came in order to see you.” Önce and sonra mark temporal relationships instead.

questions.prompt: Choose “after eating” as a verb-based temporal phrase.
questions.explanation: The pattern verb + -DIktAn sonra means “after doing”: yedikten sonra = “after eating.” The suffixes attach to the verb stem.

questions.prompt: Choose “before going home.”
questions.explanation: Before an action, Turkish uses the negative converb -mAdAn followed by önce: eve gitmeden önce = “before going home.”

questions.prompt: Choose “He entered and sat down” using -(y)Ip.
questions.explanation: Girip joins gir- (“enter”) to oturdu (“sat down”) with the converb -(y)Ip, linking successive actions by the same subject. Girerken means “while entering.”

questions.prompt: Choose “He left without saying anything.”
questions.explanation: The converb -mAdAn means “without doing”: hiçbir şey söylemeden means “without saying anything.” It marks an action not performed.

questions.prompt: Choose “She entered laughing,” using the -(y)ArAk converb.
questions.explanation: Gülerek uses the converb -(y)ArAk to describe how she entered: “laughing / with a laugh.” Gülmeden means “without laughing”; güldükten sonra means “after laughing.”

questions.prompt: Complete: “He works as a teacher.” Öğretmen ___ çalışıyor.
questions.explanation: Olarak means “as / in the capacity of,” so öğretmen olarak çalışıyor means “works as a teacher.” Gibi means “like” and does not specify the actual job role.

questions.prompt: Choose the verbal noun meaning “swimming” in “Swimming is good.”
questions.explanation: Yüzmek is the infinitive formed with -mAk and can function as the subject of a sentence: “Swimming is good.” Yüzüyorum is a finite verb meaning “I am swimming.”

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the dative-marked verbal noun meaning “I am glad you came.”
questions.explanation: Sevinmek (“be glad”) selects a dative complement: gel-me-n-e → gelmene (“at your coming”). Gelmeni is accusative and fits other verbs, such as istemek, not this construction.

questions.prompt: Which letter is part of the Turkish alphabet?
questions.explanation: Turkish has ğ but not q, w, or x in its standard alphabet.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the Turkish dotless vowel ı?
questions.explanation: Kız contains the dotless vowel ı. Turkish distinguishes ı from dotted i as separate vowels; kitap has dotted i, while gül has ü and ev has e.

questions.prompt: How do you write 47 in Turkish?
questions.explanation: Forty is kırk and seven is yedi. Turkish writes 47 as kırk yedi, with the tens before the units.

questions.prompt: How do you write 125 in Turkish?
questions.explanation: Turkish forms 125 as yüz (one hundred) + yirmi (twenty) + beş (five): yüz yirmi beş. The units follow the tens.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural of okul.
questions.explanation: Okul has the back vowel u, so its plural suffix is -lar, not -ler: okul + lar → okullar. The suffix follows two-way vowel harmony.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben öğretmen___.
questions.explanation: First-person singular nominal predicate after a consonant takes -im.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz Türk___.
questions.explanation: Türk has front rounded ü, so first-person plural is Türküz.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben hasta___.
questions.explanation: After a vowel, first-person singular nominal predicate uses buffer y: hastayım.

questions.prompt: Complete for absence at the present time: Buzdolabında süt ___. (There is no milk in the fridge now.)
questions.explanation: Yok means “there is not / there are not” in the present: buzdolabında süt yok. Vardı means “there was,” while yoktu means “there was not.”

questions.prompt: Ask whether there is water: Su ___?
questions.explanation: The question particle is written separately and follows vowel harmony. Because var has back unrounded a, the correct form is var mı?, not mi, mu, or mü.

questions.prompt: Complete: beş → ___. (fifth)
questions.explanation: The ordinal suffix follows four-way vowel harmony: beş ends with front unrounded e, so -inci yields beşinci (“fifth”), not -ıncı, -uncu, or -üncü.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sen şimdi çalışıyor ___?
questions.explanation: The question particle follows the final vowel of çalışıyor: musun.

questions.prompt: Complete: Öğretmen öğrenciler___ bir soru sordu. (to the students)
questions.explanation: The recipient of sormak (“ask”) takes the dative: öğrenci + -ler + -e → öğrencilere (“to the students”). -de marks location and -den marks source.

questions.prompt: Complete the dative suffix, including any buffer consonant: Ankara’___ gidiyorum.
questions.explanation: Ankara ends in vowel a, so the dative suffix needs buffer y: Ankara + -ya → Ankara’ya (“to Ankara”). The plain -a option omits the required buffer consonant.

questions.prompt: Complete: Anahtar masa___ . (The key is on the table.)
questions.explanation: Masa takes locative -da: masada.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ev___ kalıyorum.
questions.explanation: Ev has the front vowel e, so the locative suffix is -de: ev + de → evde (“at home”). The locative answers “where?”

questions.prompt: Complete: Çocuk okul___ geliyor. (from school)
questions.explanation: Ablative marks the point of departure: okuldan.

questions.prompt: Complete: Park___ çıktık. (We left the park.)
questions.explanation: After voiceless k, ablative uses t: parktan.

questions.prompt: Complete: Akşam___ kadar çalışacağım. (until evening)
questions.explanation: Kadar meaning until takes dative: akşama kadar.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dersten ___ eve gidiyorum.
questions.explanation: -DEn sonra means after; dersten sonra is after class.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim göz___ . (my eye)
questions.explanation: Göz takes first-person possessive -üm: gözüm.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu sizin ev___ . (your [plural/polite] house)
questions.explanation: Second-person plural possessive: eviniz.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ayşe’nin araba___ kırmızı.
questions.explanation: Third-person possessive after vowel-final araba uses s: arabası.

questions.prompt: Choose the genitive–possessive construction for “the door of a particular school” (not the general compound “school door”).
questions.explanation: Specific possession takes genitive okulun + possessive kapısı.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct bare noun phrase meaning “beautiful houses” (no case or possessive suffix).
questions.explanation: Adjectives do not agree in number with nouns in Turkish.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben çocuk___ burada yaşıyordum. (when I was a child)
questions.explanation: Çocukken means “when [someone] was a child”: çocuk + -ken. In Ben çocukken, ben makes the subject “I.”

questions.prompt: Complete: şeker + -siz → ___.
questions.explanation: The suffix -sIz follows four-way vowel harmony: şekersiz.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dün ___ okudum. (I read the specific book.)
questions.explanation: A specific direct object takes accusative: kitabı.

questions.prompt: Complete the time adjective: Dün___ toplantı uzundu. (“Yesterday’s meeting was long.”)
questions.explanation: The temporal modifier is dünkü (with rounded vowel ü).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct future tense of gitmek (ben).
questions.explanation: The stem t softens to d before the future suffix: gideceğim.

questions.prompt: Use the aorist (geniş zaman): Ben her sabah kahve ___ . (I drink coffee every morning.)
questions.explanation: The aorist içerim expresses a habitual action.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sen yüzebilir ___?
questions.explanation: The ability verb yüzebilir takes question particle misin.

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: Yağmur yağıyor, ___ dışarı çıkmıyorum.
questions.explanation: Bu yüzden introduces a result: it is raining, so I am not going out.

questions.prompt: Complete: O, öğretmen ___ çalışıyor.
questions.explanation: Öğretmen olarak means working as a teacher.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only back vowels?
questions.explanation: The Turkish back vowels are a, ı, o, u. Both a and ı belong to that set; e, i, ö, and ü are front vowels.

questions.prompt: Complete: kitap + -da → ___.
questions.explanation: After voiceless p, locative d becomes t.

questions.prompt: Complete: kitap + -(y)I → ___.
questions.explanation: Final p softens to b before the vowel-initial accusative ending.

questions.prompt: Complete: araba + third-person possessive → ___.
questions.explanation: The buffer consonant s appears before third-person possessive -ı.

questions.prompt: Choose the neutral subject–object–verb (SOV) word order for “Ali is reading a book.”
questions.explanation: Neutral Turkish word order is subject–object–verb.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct Turkish way to say “October 18, 2026” as a written date?
questions.explanation: In Turkish written dates, the day precedes the month.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative nominal sentence: Ben doktor ___.
questions.explanation: Ben doktor değilim means I am not a doctor.

questions.prompt: Complete the present continuous: başlamak → Ben şimdi ___.
questions.explanation: Başla- loses its final a before -(I)yor: başlıyorum.

questions.prompt: Complete the dative: kitap → kitab___.
questions.explanation: Kitap becomes kitaba with p → b before vowel-initial dative -a.

questions.prompt: Complete the ablative: şehir → şehir___.
questions.explanation: The last vowel i is front, so şehirden takes -den.

questions.prompt: Which phrase correctly means “after class”?
questions.explanation: Sonra follows the ablative: dersten sonra.

questions.prompt: Which correctly means “Ayşe’s bag”?
questions.explanation: A definite possessive compound marks the possessor with genitive and the possessed noun with possessive.

questions.prompt: Which is an adjective + noun phrase, rather than a noun compound?
questions.explanation: Büyük modifies ev as an adjective; the other phrases are noun compounds.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz dün saat sekizde çalışıyor___.
questions.explanation: Biz çalışıyorduk is first-person plural past continuous.

questions.prompt: Choose the natural translation of “Ali and Ayşe.”
questions.explanation: İle can join two nouns and mean and/with.

questions.prompt: Which means “the one in the room”?
questions.explanation: Odada + ki forms odadaki, a modifier/pronoun meaning the one in the room.

questions.prompt: Complete the past future-intention form: Ben bugün gidecek___ ama planım değişti. (I was going to go today, but my plans changed.)
questions.explanation: Gidecektim is first-person singular future-in-the-past.

questions.prompt: Complete using the negative future-in-the-past: O gel___ti. (He/she was not going to come.)
questions.explanation: Gel- takes the negative future form gelmeyecekti.

questions.prompt: Complete the expression meaning “in my opinion”: Bana ___ bu kolay.
questions.explanation: Bana göre is “in my opinion.” The postposition göre follows the dative pronoun bana, not the nominative ben.

questions.prompt: Complete the equal-degree comparison: Senin ___ hızlı koşuyorum. (I run as fast as you do.)
questions.explanation: Kadar can mark equality of degree: senin kadar hızlı.

questions.prompt: Complete: Meğer o doktor ___. (Apparently he/she was not a doctor.)
questions.explanation: Değilmiş expresses an inferred or reported negative nominal predicate.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported nominal question: O öğrenci ___?
questions.explanation: Öğrenci miymiş? asks whether someone was apparently a student.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ali çalış___muş. (Apparently Ali was not working.)
questions.explanation: Çalışmıyormuş is the negative reported present continuous.

questions.prompt: Which question uses the reported past form of the present continuous to ask “Was she apparently sleeping?”
questions.explanation: Uyuyor muymuş asks a reported/inferred present-continuous question.

questions.prompt: Which question uses the reported form of the future tense to ask “Was he apparently going to come?”
questions.explanation: Gelecek miymiş is a reported future question.

questions.prompt: Use the aorist (geniş zaman): Ben her gün kitap ___ . (I read every day.)
questions.explanation: Oku- takes -r in the aorist: okurum.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz Türkçe konuşabil___. (We can speak Turkish.)
questions.explanation: Konuşabiliriz is first-person plural ability in the aorist.

questions.prompt: Complete: Eskiden et ye___. (I did not use to eat meat.)
questions.explanation: Yemezdim is the negative habitual past.

questions.prompt: A friend told you that someone used to live here. Complete with the reported habitual form: Eskiden burada yaşar___.
questions.explanation: Yaşarmış expresses a reported past habit.

questions.prompt: Complete: O eskiden kahve iç___miş. (Apparently he/she did not use to drink coffee.)
questions.explanation: İçmezmiş is the negative reported aorist.

questions.prompt: Choose the complete nested genitive–possessive phrase meaning “the door of the school’s library”.
questions.explanation: Chained possessives mark both school → library and library → door.

questions.prompt: Complete the second-person possessive verbal noun: Senin erken gel___ için taksi çağırdım. (I called a taxi so that you could arrive early.)
questions.explanation: Gel-me-n forms the second-person singular possessive verbal noun gelmen; senin agrees with the possessive marking.

questions.prompt: Complete using the -mek üzere purpose construction: Sizinle görüşmek ___ geldim. (I came to meet you.)
questions.explanation: -mek üzere expresses purpose or intention.

questions.prompt: Complete: Yemek ye___ sonra çıktık. (After eating, we left.)
questions.explanation: Yedikten sonra uses -DIK + ablative -tAn.

questions.prompt: Complete: Evden çık___ önce anahtarı aldım. (Before leaving home...)
questions.explanation: Çıkmadan önce means before leaving; the -mAdAn form is required.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kahvaltı yap___ işe gittim. (I had breakfast and went to work.)
questions.explanation: Yap- takes the converb -ıp after back unrounded a.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kahve iç___ çıktım. (I left without drinking coffee.)
questions.explanation: İçmeden is iç- (drink) + -meden (“without doing”); kahve içmeden çıktım means “I left without drinking coffee.”

questions.prompt: Complete: Eve koş___ geldim. (I came home running.)
questions.explanation: Koşarak expresses manner, with -arak after the back vowel o.

questions.prompt: Which sentence naturally means “Swimming is good”?
questions.explanation: The infinitive -mek can function as a nominal subject.

questions.prompt: Complete: Senin gel___ beni mutlu etti. (Your coming made me happy.)
questions.explanation: Gelmen is gel-me + second-person possessive -n.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct suffix for göz + plural.
questions.explanation: The final vowel ö is front, selecting -ler.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains two voiceless Turkish consonants?
questions.explanation: Both ç and p are voiceless. In the other pairs, d, g, and b are voiced, although t, k, and f are voiceless.

questions.prompt: Complete: burun + my → ___.
questions.explanation: Burun loses its second vowel before the first-person possessive: burnum.

questions.prompt: Complete: ağız + accusative → ___.
questions.explanation: Ağız loses its second vowel before the accusative: ağzı.

questions.prompt: Complete: bu + dative → ___.
questions.explanation: Demonstrative bu uses pronominal n before the dative: buna.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct bare adjective–noun phrase meaning “a new car” (not a complete sentence).
questions.explanation: An adjective ordinarily precedes its noun.

questions.prompt: In “çok güzel ev”, which word is the head noun?
questions.explanation: Ev is the head noun; çok güzel modifies it.

questions.prompt: Which means “It is half past four”?
questions.explanation: Saat dört buçuk means 4:30: buçuk means “half” after the hour. Saat beşe çeyrek var is 4:45, and dördü çeyrek geçiyor is 4:15.

questions.prompt: Complete the suggestion: Yarın sahilde yürüyüş yap___! (Let’s take a walk.)
questions.explanation: Yapalım is the first-person plural optative form.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative first-person plural suggestion: “Let’s not go.”
questions.explanation: Gitmeyelim uses -mA plus the first-person plural optative ending.

questions.prompt: Which word means “in Turkish” (as a language)?
questions.explanation: The equative suffix -CA forms language names, as in Türkçe.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “This room is as big as that room.”

options.text: Bu oda o oda kadar büyük.

questions.explanation: Kadar expresses equality of degree; -DAn alone can mark a comparison.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains the present-time third-person predicate ending -DIr (which can convey inference in context)?
questions.explanation: Ali şimdi evdedir contains the third-person predicate ending -dir. Depending on context, -DIr may convey a supposition or a formal assertion; the suffix alone does not force an inferential reading.

questions.prompt: Complete the formal inference: Ayşe şu anda okulda___ .
questions.explanation: The third-person -DIr follows the locative predicate: okuldadır.

questions.prompt: Someone tells you about a former habit you did not witness. Choose the reported form.
questions.explanation: -ArmIş marks a reported or inferred habitual situation.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct nested possessive phrase for “the door of my friend’s house”?
questions.explanation: Nested genitive and possessive marking gives arkadaşımın evinin kapısı.

questions.prompt: Which Turkish sentence explicitly identifies YOU as the person who should arrive early: “What can I do so that you arrive early?”

options.text: Senin erken gelmen için ne yapabilirim?
Benim erken gelmem için ne yapabilirim?
Onun erken gelmesi için ne yapabilirim?

questions.explanation: Senin erken gelmen için explicitly makes sen the subject of the nominalized action; the other options change or omit that subject.

questions.prompt: It is 8:59 and the meeting starts at 9:00. Complete with the construction meaning “about to”: Toplantı başla___ .
questions.explanation: Başlamak üzere expresses an imminent or intended action.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dışarı çık___ önce anahtarını al. (Before going out, take your key.)
questions.explanation: Çıkmadan önce means before going out.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the reduplicated -A converb koşa koşa (running repeatedly/continuously), not the single -ArAk converb koşarak?
questions.explanation: Koşa koşa expresses repeated or sustained running.

questions.prompt: Complete the paired -A converb: Çocuklar parkta ___ vakit geçirdi. (The children spent time cheerfully, laughing and playing.)
questions.explanation: Güle oynaya is a natural paired -A converb expression meaning cheerfully or joyfully.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains the reduplicated converb ağlaya ağlaya (crying repeatedly or continuously)?
questions.explanation: Ağlaya ağlaya is a reduplicated converb expressing prolonged crying.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I know that Ayşe came.”
questions.explanation: The embedded clause uses a verbal noun with possessive and accusative marking: geldiğini.

questions.prompt: Which correctly reports “The teacher told me to sit down”?
questions.explanation: The reported instruction can be expressed with a nominalized verb and possessive/accusative marking.

questions.prompt: Choose “The teacher told us to wait.”
questions.explanation: Beklememizi marks the people expected to wait as first-person plural.

questions.prompt: Which word normally keeps its final consonant unchanged when a vowel-initial case suffix is added?
questions.explanation: Saat takes saati; the other examples show consonant softening.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accusative form of fikir (idea).
questions.explanation: Some loanwords undergo vowel loss before vowel-initial suffixes: fikir → fikri.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accusative form of hak (right, entitlement).
questions.explanation: Hak becomes hakkı with consonant gemination in this inflection.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim ___ . (This is my right.)
questions.explanation: Hak + first-person possessive -ım yields hakkım with gemination.

questions.prompt: Complete with the definite past (-DI): Dün akşam annemi ___ (aramak, ben).
questions.explanation: Aramak takes -dı + -m in the definite past: aradım.

questions.prompt: Complete with the definite past (-DI): Geçen hafta müzeye ___ (gitmek, biz).
questions.explanation: Gitmek takes the definite past form gittik for first-person plural.

questions.prompt: Use the negative definite past (-DI): Dün akşam televizyon ___ (izlemek, ben, negative).
questions.explanation: The negative definite past is izle-me-di-m → izlemedim.

questions.prompt: Use the negative definite past (-DI): Geçen pazar dışarı ___ (çıkmak, biz, negative).
questions.explanation: The negative definite past for biz is çıkmadık.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past (-DI) nominal sentence meaning “I was tired yesterday” (stated as a directly known fact).
questions.explanation: Yorgun + past copular ending -dum forms yorgundum.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past (-DI) nominal sentence meaning “We were at school yesterday” (stated as a directly known fact).
questions.explanation: The past copular form for biz is okuldaydık.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past (-DI) question meaning “Were they at work yesterday?”
questions.explanation: The question particle plus past copula and third-person plural gives miydiler.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past (-DI) question meaning “Was she ill yesterday?”
questions.explanation: The past copular question is mıydı for third-person singular.

questions.prompt: Use past continuous (-Iyor + -DI): Dün saat sekizde kitap ___ (okumak, ben).
questions.explanation: Okumak takes the progressive past form okuyordum.

questions.prompt: Use past continuous (-Iyor + -DI): Dün bu saatte yemek ___ (yapmak, biz).
questions.explanation: Yapmak takes the past progressive form yapıyorduk.

questions.prompt: Complete with -ken (“when I was a child”): Çocuk___ burada oturuyordum.
questions.explanation: Çocukken means “when (I was) a child.”

questions.prompt: Complete with -ken (“while at school”): Okulda___ çok kitap okuyordum.
questions.explanation: Okuldayken means “while at school”; the buffer y joins the vowel-final locative form to -ken.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly suffixed, single-word expression meaning “by train” (-le/-la).
questions.explanation: Tren + -(y)lA forms trenle (“by train”).

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly suffixed, single-word expression meaning “by car” (-yle/-yla).
questions.explanation: Araba + -(y)lA forms arabayla (“by car”).

questions.prompt: Addressing several people politely, complete: Lütfen burada ___ (beklemek).
questions.explanation: Bekleyin is the polite/plural second-person imperative.

questions.prompt: Addressing one person formally, complete: Lütfen kapıyı ___ (kapatmak).
questions.explanation: Kapatın is the formal second-person imperative.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative polite command: “Please do not enter.”
questions.explanation: Girmeyin uses the negative imperative for polite/plural second person.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative polite command: “Please do not wait here.”
questions.explanation: Beklemeyin is the polite negative imperative.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective suffix meaning “with salt”: Tuz___ çorba istiyorum.
questions.explanation: Tuzlu means “salty/with salt”; -lI follows vowel harmony.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective suffix meaning “without milk”: Süt___ kahve istiyorum.
questions.explanation: Sütsüz means “without milk”; -sIz follows vowel harmony.

questions.prompt: Complete with the first-person plural suggestion: Haydi biraz ___ (dinlenmek).
questions.explanation: Dinlenelim is dinlen- (rest) + -elim, the first-person plural suggestion ending. With haydi, it means “let’s rest.”

questions.prompt: Complete with the first-person plural suggestion: Haydi birlikte yemek ___ (yapmak).
questions.explanation: Yapalım is yap- (do/make) + -alım, the first-person plural suggestion ending. Haydi birlikte yemek yapalım means “Let’s cook together.”

questions.prompt: Complete the comparative: İzmir, Ankara’___ daha sıcak.
questions.explanation: The ablative -dan marks the comparison standard: Ankara’dan.

questions.prompt: Complete the comparative: Bu çanta, o çanta___ daha ağır.
questions.explanation: The ablative -dan marks the comparison standard: o çantadan.

questions.prompt: Choose the superlative expression to complete the sentence: “This is the most expensive restaurant.” Bu, ___ pahalı restoran.
questions.explanation: En + adjective expresses a superlative: en pahalı.

questions.prompt: Complete the superlative: Sınıfın ___ genç öğrencisi kim? (Who is the youngest student?)
questions.explanation: En immediately before an adjective makes a superlative: en genç = “youngest.” Daha genç means “younger,” a comparative.

questions.prompt: Complete the definite object: Şu elma___ yedim. (I ate that particular apple.)
questions.explanation: The definite accusative after vowel-final elma is -(y)ı: elmayı.

questions.prompt: Complete the definite object: Bu kapı___ kapat. (Close this door.)
questions.explanation: The definite accusative after kapı is -(y)ı: kapıyı.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I saw the child” with a definite object.
questions.explanation: The definite accusative of çocuk is çocuğu (k softens to ğ).

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I read the newspaper” with a definite object.
questions.explanation: Gazeteyi is the definite accusative of gazete.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I bought some bread” without identifying a specific loaf.
questions.explanation: Bare ekmek is a nonspecific object (“some bread”); bu ekmeği and o ekmeği refer to specified bread, while ekmeği has accusative marking.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I read a novel” without specifying which novel.
questions.explanation: Bir roman without accusative supports a nonspecific reading.

questions.prompt: Complete with the locative relative suffix -DAki (the children who are in the park): Park___ çocuklar oynuyor.
questions.explanation: Parktaki means “in the park” and modifies çocuklar: “the children in the park.”

questions.prompt: Complete with the locative relative suffix -DAki (the cat that is in the house): Ev___ kedi uyuyor.
questions.explanation: Evdeki modifies kedi: “the cat in the house.”

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “Ayşe is coming too.”
questions.explanation: Additive de (“too”) is written separately: Ayşe de geliyor.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct spelling meaning “We also want tea.”
questions.explanation: Additive de is separate from the pronoun biz.

questions.prompt: Use the future tense (-AcAk): Yarın seni ___ (aramak, ben).
questions.explanation: Ara- + -(y)acak + first-person singular gives arayacağım.

questions.prompt: Use the future tense (-AcAk): Gelecek hafta İstanbul’a ___ (gitmek, biz).
questions.explanation: Future first-person plural of gitmek is gideceğiz.

questions.prompt: Express a past intention that did not happen: Dün sana mesaj ___ ama telefonum bozuldu. (atmak, ben, future-in-the-past)
questions.explanation: Atacaktım expresses “I was going to send” in a past plan.

questions.prompt: Express a past plan that changed: Dün erken ___ ama işim uzadı. (çıkmak, ben, future-in-the-past)
questions.explanation: Çıkacaktım means “I was going to leave.”

questions.prompt: Complete “In my opinion, this is easy”: ___ göre bu kolay.
questions.explanation: Bana göre means “according to me” or “in my opinion.” Göre requires the dative form bana, not the nominative ben.

questions.prompt: Complete “According to you, which is better?”: ___ göre hangisi daha iyi?
questions.explanation: Sana göre means “according to you / in your opinion.”

questions.prompt: You wake up and see wet streets, so you infer that it rained overnight. Complete with inferential past (-mIş): Dün gece yağmur ___ . (yağmak)
questions.explanation: Yağmış marks a conclusion based on evidence rather than directly witnessed rain.

questions.prompt: You find an empty plate and infer someone ate the cake. Use -mIş: Pastayı biri ___! (yemek)
questions.explanation: Yemiş signals an inference from evidence.

questions.prompt: Complete with reported future (-AcAk + -mIş): Duyduğuma göre yarın hava güzel ___ . (olmak)
questions.explanation: Olacakmış is a future form reported secondhand.

questions.prompt: Complete with reported future (-AcAk + -mIş): Söylediklerine göre tren geç ___ . (gelmek)
questions.explanation: Gelecekmiş reports a future event learned indirectly.

questions.prompt: The phone is switched off, so you guess the person is busy. Use conjectural -DIr: Telefonu kapalı; şimdi meşgul___ .
questions.explanation: Meşguldür expresses a conjecture; ü harmonizes with meşgul.

questions.prompt: It is late, so you guess the children are sleeping. Use conjectural -DIr: Saat geç; çocuklar uyuyor___ .
questions.explanation: Uyuyordur combines progressive -yor with conjectural -dur.

questions.prompt: Use the habitual aorist (geniş zaman): Her hafta sonu kitap ___ (okumak, ben).
questions.explanation: The affirmative aorist of okumak in first-person singular is okurum.

questions.prompt: Use the habitual aorist (geniş zaman): Babam her sabah erken ___ (kalkmak).
questions.explanation: Kalkmak takes -ar in the third-person singular aorist: kalkar.

questions.prompt: Choose the ability form -(y)Abil: Ben bisiklet ___ . (I know how to ride a bicycle.)
questions.explanation: Sürebilirim expresses ability to ride, not merely an action in progress.

questions.prompt: Choose the -(y)Abil ability form: Ayşe İngilizce ___ . (Ayşe is able to speak English.)
questions.explanation: Konuşabilir is the third-person singular affirmative ability/aorist form.

questions.prompt: Use the habitual past (-ArDI): Çocukken her yaz köye ___ (gitmek, biz).
questions.explanation: Giderdik describes a repeated past habit: we used to go.

questions.prompt: Use the habitual past (-ArDI): Eskiden her akşam yürüyüş ___ (yapmak, o).
questions.explanation: Yapardı marks an action habitually performed in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose the conjunction that introduces a reason: Dışarı çıkmadık, ___ yağmur yağıyordu.
questions.explanation: Çünkü introduces the reason: because it was raining.

questions.prompt: Complete with the causal conjunction: Bugün erken yatacağım, ___ çok yorgunum.
questions.explanation: Çünkü explicitly supplies the reason for going to bed early.

questions.prompt: Complete the purpose clause using -mAk için: Seni gör___ için buraya geldim.
questions.explanation: Görmek için means in order to see; the infinitive ending is -mek.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning “in order to learn Turkish.”
questions.explanation: Öğrenmek için is an infinitive plus için purpose construction.

questions.prompt: Complete with the -DIktAn sonra construction (after doing something): Eve gel___ sonra yemek yedim.
questions.explanation: Geldikten sonra means after coming home.

questions.prompt: Choose the expression meaning “after finishing the lesson.”
questions.explanation: Bitirdikten sonra specifies that the lesson was finished before the next action.

questions.prompt: Complete using the -(y)Ip converb to link two sequential actions: Eve dön___ dinlendim.
questions.explanation: Dönüp dinlendim means I returned home and then rested.

questions.prompt: Use the -(y)Ip converb to link two sequential actions: Kapıyı aç___ içeri girdi.
questions.explanation: Açıp is the -(y)Ip converb of açmak; it links opening the door to the following action, entering.

questions.prompt: Use the -(y)ArAk manner converb, meaning “laughing as they entered”: Çocuk gül___ odaya girdi.
questions.explanation: Gülerek means laughing, describing how the child entered.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence using -(y)ArAk to describe how someone went to work.
questions.explanation: Yürüyerek indicates the manner of going to work: on foot.

questions.prompt: Use the -mA verbal noun with accusative marking: Yüz___ çok seviyorum. (I love swimming.)
questions.explanation: Yüzmeyi is the -mA verbal noun with accusative -(y)I, as the object of seviyorum.

questions.prompt: Choose the -mA verbal noun with accusative marking: Kitap oku___ seviyorum. (I enjoy reading books.)
questions.explanation: Okumayı combines the -mA verbal noun with accusative -(y)I.

questions.prompt: Use the possessed -mA verbal noun with accusative marking: Müdür çalışanlardan erken gel___ istedi. (The manager wanted the employees to come early.)
questions.explanation: Gelmelerini is a possessive-marked verbal noun with accusative in the reported request.

questions.prompt: Use the possessed -mA verbal noun with accusative marking: Anne çocuklarına odalarını temizle___ söyledi. (The mother told her children to clean their rooms.)
questions.explanation: Temizlemelerini is the possessed verbal noun in accusative, referring to the children’s action.

questions.prompt: Which word contains only back vowels (a, ı, o, u)?
questions.explanation: Okul contains o and u, both back vowels.

questions.prompt: Which word contains only front vowels (e, i, ö, ü)?
questions.explanation: Gözlük contains ö and ü, both front vowels.

questions.prompt: Choose the plural of “kitap.”
questions.explanation: The plural suffix after a back vowel is -lar: kitaplar.

questions.prompt: Choose the plural of “gün.”
questions.explanation: The plural suffix after a front vowel is -ler: günler.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative nominal predicate (I am not tired): Ben yorgun ___.
questions.explanation: Yorgun değilim means “I am not tired”; değil takes the first-person singular ending -im.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I am not a teacher.”
questions.explanation: The first-person singular nominal negation is öğretmen değilim.

questions.prompt: Complete the yes/no question: Sen doktor ___? (Are you a doctor?)
questions.explanation: The last vowel of doktor is o, so the question particle is mu; with second-person singular it becomes musun.

questions.prompt: Complete the question: Sen Türk ___? (Are you Turkish?)
questions.explanation: The final vowel in Türk is ü, which requires müsün.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz öğrenci___. (We are students.)
questions.explanation: A vowel-final predicate takes the buffer y: öğrenciyiz.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz mutlu___. (We are happy.)
questions.explanation: Mutlu ends in u and takes the first-person plural ending -yuz: mutluyuz.

questions.prompt: Complete with a neutral present-time existential: Çantamda bir kalem ___. (There is a pen in my bag now.)
questions.explanation: Var indicates that something exists or is present.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “There is no milk in the refrigerator.”
questions.explanation: Yok expresses nonexistence: Buzdolabında süt yok.

questions.prompt: Choose the ordinal meaning “fifth.”
questions.explanation: Beşinci is the ordinal “fifth”: beş (five) + -inci. Turkish ordinal suffixes follow four-way vowel harmony.

questions.prompt: Choose the ordinal meaning “second.”
questions.explanation: İkinci means “second”; iki is the cardinal “two.”

questions.prompt: Complete with the present continuous (-Iyor): Şu anda kitap ___. (I am reading a book right now.)
questions.explanation: The verb okumak forms okuyorum in the present continuous: oku- + -yor + -um. The y is part of the present-continuous form, not an independently inserted buffer consonant.

questions.prompt: Complete using the present continuous (-Iyor): Şimdi müzik ___. (We are listening to music.)
questions.explanation: Dinle- forms dinliyor- in the present continuous; first-person plural gives dinliyoruz.

questions.prompt: Complete using the negative present continuous (-mIyor): Şu anda televizyon ___. (I am not watching television.)
questions.explanation: İzle- + negative present continuous yields izlemiyorum.

questions.prompt: Complete using the negative present continuous (-mIyor): Şimdi kahve ___. (We are not drinking coffee right now.)
questions.explanation: The negative present continuous first-person plural of içmek is içmiyoruz.

questions.prompt: Complete the destination case: Yarın İzmir’___ gidiyoruz.
questions.explanation: A destination takes the dative: İzmir’e.

questions.prompt: Complete the destination case: Bu akşam sinema___ gidiyorum.
questions.explanation: Sinema ends in a vowel, so the dative takes buffer -y-: sinemaya.

questions.prompt: Complete the locative case: Anahtar çanta___. (The key is in the bag.)
questions.explanation: Çanta has a back vowel a and ends in a vowel, so it takes locative -da: çanta + da → çantada (“in the bag”).

questions.prompt: Complete the locative case: Çocuk park___ oynuyor. (The child is playing in the park.)
questions.explanation: After voiceless k, locative -da becomes -ta: parkta.

questions.prompt: Complete the ablative case: İş___ eve dönüyorum. (I am returning home from work.)
questions.explanation: After voiceless ş, the ablative is -ten: işten.

questions.prompt: Complete the ablative case: Ankara’___ geliyorum. (I am coming from Ankara.)
questions.explanation: Ankara takes ablative -dan: Ankara’dan.

questions.prompt: Complete the “before” construction: Toplantı___ önce yemek yiyelim. (Let’s eat before the meeting.)
questions.explanation: -DAn önce expresses “before”: toplantıdan önce.

questions.prompt: Complete the “before” construction: İş___ önce kahve içiyorum. (I drink coffee before work.)
questions.explanation: After voiceless ş, -DAn önce becomes işten önce.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “It is half past seven.”
questions.explanation: Saat yedi buçuk is 7:30. Yediyi çeyrek geçiyor is 7:15; sekize çeyrek var is 7:45.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “It is quarter to nine.”
questions.explanation: Saat dokuza çeyrek var means fifteen minutes remain until nine.

questions.prompt: Complete: Tren saat beşi çeyrek ___ kalkıyor. (The train leaves at 5:15.)
questions.explanation: With clock time + accusative numeral, çeyrek geçe expresses a quarter past the hour for an event time.

questions.prompt: Complete: Film saat sekize çeyrek ___ başlıyor. (The film starts at 7:45.)
questions.explanation: With the hour in the dative, çeyrek kala expresses a quarter to the hour for an event time.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim kitab___. (This is my book.)
questions.explanation: Kitap takes the first-person singular possessive suffix -ım: kitabım, with p becoming b before the vowel-initial suffix.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim ev___. (This is my house.)
questions.explanation: The first-person singular possessive suffix after ev is -im: evim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu onun çanta___. (This is his/her bag.)
questions.explanation: A vowel-final noun takes the third-person singular possessive suffix -sı: çantası.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu onun ev___. (This is his/her house.)
questions.explanation: A consonant-final noun takes the third-person singular possessive suffix -i here: evi.

questions.prompt: Supply the full genitive suffix after the apostrophe: Ayşe’___ telefonu çalıyor. (Ayşe’s phone is ringing.)
questions.explanation: Ayşe ends in the front vowel e. Add buffer n and the front-vowel genitive ending -in: Ayşe’nin telefonu çalıyor.

questions.prompt: Supply the genitive suffix after the apostrophe: Mehmet’___ arabası yeni. (Mehmet’s car is new.)
questions.explanation: Mehmet ends in a consonant, so no buffer consonant is needed. Its last vowel e requires the front-vowel genitive -in: Mehmet’in arabası.

questions.prompt: Complete the noun compound: elma su___ . (Apple juice.)
questions.explanation: The compound elma suyu uses the third-person possessive marker -(s)I; su takes the irregular linking y: suyu.

questions.prompt: Complete the noun compound: çocuk kitab___. (A children’s book.)
questions.explanation: In the indefinite noun compound çocuk kitabı, kitap takes the third-person possessive suffix -ı and p softens to b.

questions.prompt: Choose the bare adjective + noun phrase for “a big garden,” without a possessive suffix.
questions.explanation: In a basic adjective–noun phrase, the adjective precedes the noun: büyük bahçe.

questions.prompt: Choose the bare adjective + noun phrase for “a new book,” without a possessive suffix.
questions.explanation: An attributive adjective precedes its noun: yeni kitap.

questions.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Did you see Ali yesterday?”
questions.explanation: Gördün mü asks the second-person singular definite-past yes/no question.

questions.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Did you drink tea this morning?”
questions.explanation: İçtin mi is the second-person singular definite-past question form.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past third-person singular form: “He/she arrived.” (gelmek)
questions.explanation: Gelmek forms the third-person singular definite past as geldi.

questions.prompt: Choose the definite-past third-person singular form: “He/she wrote.” (yazmak)
questions.explanation: Yazmak forms the third-person singular definite past as yazdı.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I was not tired.”
questions.explanation: Değildim negates a nominal predicate in the definite past with first-person singular agreement.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I was not at home.”
questions.explanation: Evde değildim means I was not at home; değildim is past negative nominal predication.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I was not working.”
questions.explanation: Çalışmıyordum expresses the negative past progressive, rather than a simple past or present negative.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I was not reading.”
questions.explanation: Okumuyordum is the negative past progressive first-person singular form.

questions.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Were you sleeping?”
questions.explanation: Uyuyor muydun asks a second-person singular question in the past progressive.

questions.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Were you waiting?”
questions.explanation: Bekliyor muydun asks whether someone was waiting in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I came with my sister.”
questions.explanation: The comitative/instrumental suffix -le marks with: kız kardeşimle.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I walked with my father.”
questions.explanation: Babamla uses the comitative suffix -la to mean with my father.

questions.prompt: Choose the informal singular affirmative command meaning “Sit!”
questions.explanation: Otur! is the informal singular imperative of oturmak; oturun is plural/polite and oturma is negative.

questions.prompt: Choose the informal singular negative command meaning “Don’t go!”
questions.explanation: Gitme! uses -me to make the informal singular imperative negative.

questions.prompt: Choose the third-person singular command meaning “Let him/her sit!”
questions.explanation: The third-person singular imperative takes -sIn: otursun; oturmasın is negative.

questions.prompt: Choose the third-person singular negative command meaning “Let him/her not come!”
questions.explanation: Gelmesin combines the negative -me with the third-person imperative -sin.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “salty / with salt.”
questions.explanation: The suffix -lu forms an adjective meaning containing salt: tuzlu.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “milky / containing milk.”
questions.explanation: Sütlü means containing milk, using the vowel-harmonic form -lü.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “without sugar / sugar-free.”
questions.explanation: The privative suffix -siz expresses absence: şekersiz means sugar-free.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective meaning “without milk / milk-free.”
questions.explanation: Sütsüz uses the privative suffix -süz to mean without milk.

questions.prompt: Complete the comparison “Ankara is colder than Antalya”: Ankara Antalya’___ daha soğuk.
questions.explanation: Comparisons use the ablative -DAn on the standard: Antalya’dan daha soğuk. The apostrophe separates the suffix from the proper name.

questions.prompt: Complete the comparison “This bag is heavier than that bag”: Bu çanta, o çanta___ daha ağır.
questions.explanation: After çanta, the ablative comparison ending is -dan: o çantadan daha ağır.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning “the fastest train.”
questions.explanation: En before an adjective marks the superlative: en hızlı tren.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning “the oldest house.”
questions.explanation: En eski is the superlative adjective meaning oldest.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I read the book” (a particular book).
questions.explanation: Kitabı is the definite accusative form of kitap; p softens to b before -ı.

questions.prompt: Complete “I opened the door” (a particular door): Kapı___ açtım.
questions.explanation: The definite object kapı takes the buffer y plus accusative -ı: kapıyı.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I also speak Turkish.”
questions.explanation: The separately written particle de adds also/too to ben: Ben de.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “Ayşe also came.”
questions.explanation: The additive particle de is written separately: Ayşe de geldi.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning simply “I am at school,” without “also/too.”
questions.explanation: Okuldayım is the locative okulda plus first-person predicate; separate de would mean also.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning simply “Ayşe is at home,” without “also/too.”
questions.explanation: Evde is locative (at home); the separate particle de in Ayşe de evde adds also.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “We will not come tomorrow.”
questions.explanation: Gelmeyeceğiz is first-person plural negative future: gel- + -me- (negation) + -y- (buffer) + -ecek (future) + -iz (we). Before the vowel-initial personal ending, k softens to ğ: gelmeyeceğiz.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “She will not eat.”
questions.explanation: Yemeyecek is the negative future of yemek; compare affirmative yiyecek.

questions.prompt: Choose the future-tense question meaning “Will they go tomorrow?”
questions.explanation: Gidecekler mi uses the future -ecek plus plural agreement and a separate question particle.

questions.prompt: Choose the future-tense question meaning “Will you (singular) study tonight?”
questions.explanation: Çalışacak mısın? asks a second-person singular future question.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I speak English,” using the language adverb in -ce/-ca.
questions.explanation: İngilizce is the name of the language and functions adverbially with konuşmak.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “He/she speaks German,” using the language adverb in -ce/-ca.
questions.explanation: Almanca is the German-language adverb used with konuşmak. Turkish konuşuyor has no grammatical gender, so it can mean “he speaks” or “she speaks” according to context.

questions.prompt: Complete: “According to you, is it difficult?” ___ göre zor mu?
questions.explanation: The postposition göre takes the dative: sana göre means “according to you.”

questions.prompt: Choose “according to the teacher.”
questions.explanation: Göre follows a dative-marked noun: öğretmene göre.

questions.prompt: Choose “like a bird.”
questions.explanation: Gibi means “like/as” and follows the noun kuş without a case suffix here.

questions.prompt: Complete: Çocuk ___ koşuyor. (He/she runs like a child.)
questions.explanation: Gibi means “like/as”: çocuk gibi koşuyor means “runs like a child.” It follows the noun being compared.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently they did not see it” (reported/inferred past).
questions.explanation: Görmemişler combines negation -me with the reported/inferred past -miş and plural -ler.

questions.prompt: Complete with reported/inferred past: O dün gel___. (Apparently he/she did not come yesterday.)
questions.explanation: Gelmemiş is the negative reported/inferred past of gelmek.

questions.prompt: Choose the question in the reported/inferred past (rather than the directly witnessed past): “Have they left?”
questions.explanation: Gitmişler mi uses -miş for the reported/inferred past; mi is written separately.

questions.prompt: Choose the informal singular question in the reported/inferred past: “Have you read it?”
questions.explanation: Okumuş musun uses the reported/inferred past -muş and the question particle mu with second-person ending.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently they are students.”
questions.explanation: Öğrenciymişler expresses reported/inferred nominal information with -ymiş.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ayşe doktor___. (Apparently Ayşe is a doctor.)
questions.explanation: Doktormuş uses the reported/inferred nominal suffix -muş, matching the last vowel o in doktor.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently they are working.”
questions.explanation: Çalışıyorlarmış reports ongoing activity using -yor and reported -mış.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently she is not sleeping.”
questions.explanation: Uyumuyormuş combines present progressive negation with the reported/inferred marker.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently they will not leave.”
questions.explanation: Gitmeyeceklermiş combines negative future and reported/inferred information.

questions.prompt: Choose “Apparently she will not read.”
questions.explanation: Okumayacakmış combines future negation -ma-yacak with the reported/inferred marker -mış.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative aorist for “I generally do not eat meat.”
questions.explanation: Yemem is first-person singular negative aorist; the prompt specifies a general habit.

questions.prompt: Complete with negative aorist: Ben hafta sonları erken kalk___. (I do not generally get up early on weekends.)
questions.explanation: Kalkmam is the first-person singular negative aorist of kalkmak.

questions.prompt: Choose the aorist question “Do you usually drink tea?”
questions.explanation: İçer misin asks about a general habit with the aorist.

questions.prompt: Complete with the aorist: Sen genellikle kitap oku___?
questions.explanation: Okur musun is the aorist question; okur is formed from oku- + -r.

questions.prompt: Choose “We cannot swim” using the negative ability suffix.
questions.explanation: Yüzemeyiz expresses inability with -eme and first-person plural -yiz.

questions.prompt: Complete with negative ability: Ben piyano çal___. (I cannot play the piano.)
questions.explanation: Çalamam is the first-person singular negative ability form of çalmak.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the past habitual (-rDI) construction meaning “We used to come here every summer,” rather than the simple past.
questions.explanation: Gelirdik describes a habitual past action; her yaz supports the repeated-habit reading.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the past habitual (-rDI) construction meaning “When I was a child, I used to play in the street.”
questions.explanation: Oynardım uses the past habitual/aorist-past form; oynadım refers to a completed past event.

questions.prompt: Complete: Çok yağmur yağdı, ___ evde kaldık. (It rained a lot, so we stayed home.)
questions.explanation: Bu yüzden means “therefore/for this reason” and introduces the consequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the connector meaning “because,” not “therefore.”
questions.explanation: Çünkü introduces a reason; bu yüzden and bu nedenle introduce a result.

questions.prompt: Complete with the purpose expression -mAk üzere (not -mAk için): Sizinle konuşmak ___ geldim.
questions.explanation: Konuşmak üzere geldim means “I came in order to speak”; the infinitive is followed by üzere.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence using -mAk üzere to express purpose: “I came to pick you up.”
questions.explanation: Almak üzere expresses the purpose of coming, rather than when the action occurred.

questions.prompt: Choose “after finishing the homework” with -DIktAn sonra.
questions.explanation: Bitirdikten sonra uses the -DIktAn sonra construction for “after finishing.”

questions.prompt: Complete with -DIktAn sonra: Kahvaltı yap___ sonra dışarı çıktık.
questions.explanation: Yaptıktan sonra means “after doing”; yap- takes -tıktan after the voiceless p.

questions.prompt: Choose “before opening the door” with -mAdAn önce.
questions.explanation: Açmadan önce means “before opening”; the negative-looking -madan here forms a temporal converb.

questions.prompt: Complete with -mAdAn önce: Evden çık___ önce ışıkları kapat.
questions.explanation: Çıkmadan önce means “before leaving.”

questions.prompt: Choose “She opened the door and entered” using -(y)Ip.
questions.explanation: Açıp joins opening the door with entering, using the -(y)Ip converb.

questions.prompt: Complete using -(y)Ip: Kitabı al___ masaya koydu.
questions.explanation: Alıp links “taking the book” and “putting it on the table.”

questions.prompt: Choose “She went out without drinking tea” using -mAdAn.
questions.explanation: İçmeden expresses doing the second action without doing the first.

questions.prompt: Complete with -mAdAn: Kimseye haber ver___ ayrıldı. (He/she left without telling anyone.)
questions.explanation: Vermeden expresses “without giving/telling” in this context.

questions.prompt: Choose “He walked while smiling” using -(y)ArAk.
questions.explanation: Gülerek presents smiling as accompanying manner of walking.

questions.prompt: Complete with -(y)ArAk: Koş___ otobüse yetişti. (He/she caught the bus by running.)
questions.explanation: Koşarak expresses running as the manner or means of catching the bus.

questions.prompt: Complete with olarak to mean “as a profession”: Hastanede hemşire ___ çalışıyor.
questions.explanation: Hemşire olarak çalışıyor means “works as a nurse.”

questions.prompt: Choose “She works as a translator” using olarak.
questions.explanation: Çevirmen olarak indicates the role or capacity in which someone works.

questions.prompt: Choose the infinitive/verbal noun in “Reading is useful.”
questions.explanation: Okumak is the -mAk verbal noun meaning “reading/to read.”

questions.prompt: Complete with -mAk: Her gün yürü___ sağlıklıdır. (Walking every day is healthy.)
questions.explanation: Yürümek is the infinitive/verbal noun formed with -mek after the front vowel ü.

questions.prompt: Choose “I am glad you arrived” using a dative-marked verbal noun.
questions.explanation: Gelmene is gelme + second-person singular possessive -n + dative -e.

questions.prompt: Choose “I am glad Ayşe came” using a dative-marked verbal noun.
questions.explanation: Ayşe’nin gelmesine means “at/about Ayşe’s coming”: gelme + third-person possessive -si + dative -ne. Sevinmek takes a dative complement here.

questions.prompt: Which character is a letter of the Turkish alphabet?
questions.explanation: Ş is a Turkish alphabet letter; q, w and x are not letters in the standard Turkish alphabet.

questions.prompt: Choose the Turkish letter that represents a dotless vowel.
questions.explanation: The Turkish letter ı is a dotless vowel, distinct from dotted i.

questions.prompt: Which word contains the dotless Turkish vowel ı?
questions.explanation: Sıcak contains dotless ı; the other words do not.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelled Turkish word meaning “light.”
questions.explanation: Işık (“light”) is spelled with dotless ı at both vowel positions.

questions.prompt: How do you write 68 in Turkish?
questions.explanation: 68 is altmış sekiz: sixty plus eight.

questions.prompt: Choose the Turkish spelling of 93.
questions.explanation: Doksan means ninety and üç means three. Turkish puts tens before units: doksan üç = 93.

questions.prompt: How do you write 246 in Turkish?
questions.explanation: 246 is iki yüz (200) + kırk (40) + altı (6).

questions.prompt: Choose the Turkish spelling of 318.
questions.explanation: 318 is üç yüz (300) + on (10) + sekiz (8).

questions.prompt: Choose the plain plural of kitap (without any possessive suffix).
questions.explanation: The plural suffix follows back-vowel harmony: kitap + -lar = kitaplar.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural of şehir.
questions.explanation: The plural suffix follows front-vowel harmony: şehir + -ler = şehirler.

questions.prompt: Complete the nominal predicate: Ben doktor___. (I am a doctor.)
questions.explanation: Doktor has o as its last vowel, so the first-person singular ending is -um: doktorum.

questions.prompt: Complete the nominal predicate: Ben mühendis___. (I am an engineer.)
questions.explanation: Mühendis has i as its last vowel, so the first-person singular ending is -im: mühendisim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz doktor___. (We are doctors.)
questions.explanation: Doktor has o as its last vowel: doktoruz (we are doctors).

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz mühendis___. (We are engineers.)
questions.explanation: Mühendis has i as its last vowel: mühendisiz (we are engineers).

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben yorgun___. (I am tired.)
questions.explanation: Yorgun has u as its last vowel, so the first-person singular ending is -um: yorgunum.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben üzgün___. (I am sad.)
questions.explanation: Üzgün has ü as its last vowel, so the first-person singular ending is -üm: üzgünüm.

questions.prompt: Complete for absence right now: Masada hiç ekmek ___. (There is no bread at all on the table now.)
questions.explanation: Yok expresses nonexistence or absence: Masada hiç ekmek yok.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “There is no coffee in the cup.”
questions.explanation: Yok indicates absence; the other sentences affirm coffee exists or describe it.

questions.prompt: Complete the yes/no question asking whether there is bread: Ekmek ___?
questions.explanation: The separate question particle harmonizes with var: Ekmek var mı?

questions.prompt: Choose the present-time question meaning “Is there a bus?”
questions.explanation: Existence questions use var plus separate mı: Otobüs var mı?

questions.prompt: What is the singular ordinal form of altı (six)?
questions.explanation: The ordinal of altı is altıncı (sixth).

questions.prompt: What is the ordinal form of dört (four)?
questions.explanation: The ordinal of dört is dördüncü (fourth): the final t softens to d before the vowel-initial ordinal suffix -üncü.

questions.prompt: Complete the present progressive yes/no question: Sen kitap okuyor ___?
questions.explanation: Okuyor has o as its last vowel, so the separate question particle is mu: okuyor musun?

questions.prompt: Complete the present progressive yes/no question: Sen bizi dinliyor ___?
questions.explanation: Dinliyor has o as its last vowel; the correct form is dinliyor musun?

questions.prompt: Complete the dative suffix: Çocuklar öğretmen___ soru soruyor. (The children ask the teacher a question.)
questions.explanation: Öğretmen ends in a consonant and has a front vowel, so the dative is öğretmene.

questions.prompt: Complete the dative suffix: Babam doktor___ telefon ediyor. (My father phones the doctor.)
questions.explanation: Doktor has a back vowel and ends in a consonant, so the dative is doktora.

questions.prompt: Supply the full dative suffix after the apostrophe, including a buffer consonant if needed: Yarın Bursa’___ gidiyoruz. (We are going to Bursa tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: Bursa ends in a vowel and has a back vowel; the dative is Bursa’ya with buffer y.

questions.prompt: Supply the full dative suffix after the apostrophe: Yarın İzmir’___ gidiyoruz. (We are going to İzmir tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: İzmir ends in a consonant and has a front vowel, so the dative is İzmir’e.

questions.prompt: Complete the locative suffix: Telefon çanta___. (The phone is in the bag.)
questions.explanation: Çanta ends in a vowel and has a back vowel, so the locative is çantada.

questions.prompt: Complete the locative suffix: Kitap raf___. (The book is on the shelf.)
questions.explanation: Raf ends in voiceless f and has a back vowel, so the locative is rafta.

questions.prompt: Complete: Anahtar ev___ kaldı. (The key remained at home.)
questions.explanation: Ev has a front vowel and ends in a voiced consonant: evde.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz ev___ oturuyoruz. (We are sitting at home.)
questions.explanation: Ev takes the locative ending -de because e is a front vowel and v is voiced: ev + de → evde (“at home”). -den means “from home,” and -e means “to home.”

questions.prompt: Complete: Öğrenci okul___ çıktı. (The student came out of school.)
questions.explanation: Okuldan marks movement from school with the ablative -dan.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sabah okul___ eve geldim. (I came home from school.)
questions.explanation: Okuldan means from school; -dan is the ablative ending.

questions.prompt: Complete: Çocuk park___ koşarak çıktı. (The child ran out of the park.)
questions.explanation: Park ends in voiceless k, so the ablative is parktan.
