questions.prompt: Complete: Park___ eve yürüdük. (We walked home from the park.)
questions.explanation: The ablative suffix after park begins with t: parktan.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sabah___ kadar uyudum. (I slept until morning.)
questions.explanation: Kadar in the sense of until takes the dative: sabaha kadar.

questions.prompt: Complete: Gece___ kadar çalıştık. (We worked until night.)
questions.explanation: Geceye kadar means until night; vowel-final gece takes buffer y before -e.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kahvaltıdan ___ işe gidiyorum. (I go to work after breakfast.)
questions.explanation: The ablative + sonra construction expresses after: kahvaltıdan sonra.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dersten ___ arkadaşımı aradım. (I called my friend after class.)
questions.explanation: Sonra means “after” and commonly follows an ablative-marked noun: ders + ten + sonra → dersten sonra (“after class”).

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim söz___. (This is my word/promise.)
questions.explanation: Söz takes the first-person singular possessive suffix -üm: sözüm.

questions.prompt: Complete: Benim göz___ ağrıyor. (My eye hurts.)
questions.explanation: Gözüm is göz + -üm, following four-way vowel harmony.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu sizin kitab___. (This is your book; plural/polite you.)
questions.explanation: The softened stem kitab- takes -ınız: kitabınız.

questions.prompt: Complete: Sizin ev___ büyük. (Your [plural/polite] house is big.)
questions.explanation: Eviniz uses second-person plural/polite possessive -iniz.

questions.prompt: Complete: Mehmet’in araba___ yeni. (Mehmet’s car is new.)
questions.explanation: After vowel-final araba, third-person possessive uses buffer s: arabası.

questions.prompt: Complete: Elif’in oda___ geniş. (Elif’s room is spacious.)
questions.explanation: Oda + -sı gives odası, with third-person possessive buffer s.

questions.prompt: Which means ‘the window of a particular house’ (not a general house-window compound)?
questions.explanation: Specific possession takes evin (genitive) + penceresi (possessive).

questions.prompt: Which means ‘the garden of a particular school’ (not a generic school garden)?
questions.explanation: The genitive–possessive construction is okulun bahçesi.

questions.prompt: Choose the bare noun phrase meaning ‘new books’ (no case or possessive suffix).
questions.explanation: Turkish adjectives do not pluralize to agree with nouns: yeni kitaplar.

questions.prompt: Choose the bare noun phrase meaning ‘small rooms’ (no case or possessive suffix).
questions.explanation: Plural attaches to the noun, not the adjective: küçük odalar.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ben öğrenci___ her gün kitap okurdum. (When I was a student, I used to read daily.)
questions.explanation: The vowel-final noun öğrenci takes -yken: öğrenciyken.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz küçük___ bu sokakta oynardık. (When we were little, we played on this street.)
questions.explanation: Küçükken is küçük (“small/young”) + -ken (“when”); Biz küçükken means “when we were little.”

questions.prompt: Complete the adjective: tuz + -sIz → ___ (salt-free).
questions.explanation: Tuzsuz follows back rounded vowel harmony with -suz.

questions.prompt: Complete the adjective: yağ + -sIz → ___ (fat-free).
questions.explanation: Yağsız follows back unrounded vowel harmony with -sız.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “I saw the specific dog.”
questions.explanation: A specific direct object takes the accusative: köpek → köpeği (k softens to ğ).

questions.prompt: Complete with the simple past: Bu filmi daha önce ___. (I watched this particular film before.)
questions.explanation: Bu filmi is accusative-marked; izledim gives the stated past-tense meaning.

questions.prompt: Complete the modifier: Yarın___ sınav zor olacak. (“Tomorrow’s exam will be difficult.”)
questions.explanation: Yarınki is the standard temporal adjective meaning tomorrow’s.

questions.prompt: Which expression means “today’s newspaper”?
questions.explanation: Bugünkü is the adjective derived from bugün with -kü.

questions.prompt: Choose the standard future tense of gitmek for “we will go.”
questions.explanation: Git- softens t → d before -ecek: gideceğiz.

questions.prompt: Complete with the future tense: Ben yarın eve ___ . (I will go home tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: Gideceğim is the first-person singular future form of gitmek.

questions.prompt: Choose the aorist habitual form: O her hafta sonu kitap ___ . (He/she reads books every weekend.)
questions.explanation: Okur is the aorist form indicating a habitual action.

questions.prompt: Complete with the aorist: Biz genellikle erken ___ . (We generally get up early.)
questions.explanation: Kalkarız is the first-person plural aorist of kalkmak.

questions.prompt: Complete the ability question: Siz Türkçe konuşabilir ___? (Can you speak Turkish?)
questions.explanation: Konuşabilir takes the question particle mi + second-person plural/polite ending: misiniz.

questions.prompt: Complete: O hızlı koşabilir ___? (Can he/she run fast?)
questions.explanation: The final vowel in koşabilir is i, so the separate question particle is mi.

questions.prompt: Choose the connector that means “therefore”: Çok yorgunum, ___ erken yatacağım.
questions.explanation: Bu yüzden expresses a result: I am tired, therefore I will go to bed early.

questions.prompt: Complete with a cause connector: Evde kaldım ___ hastaydım. (I stayed home because I was ill.)
questions.explanation: Çünkü introduces the reason for staying home.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ayşe doktor ___ çalışıyor. (Ayşe works as a doctor.)
questions.explanation: Doktor olarak means in the role/capacity of a doctor.

questions.prompt: Which phrase expresses someone’s actual occupation as “a translator,” rather than merely resembling a translator?
questions.explanation: Çevirmen olarak expresses the occupational role; gibi means like/as if.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only Turkish back vowels?
questions.explanation: The four back vowels are a, ı, o and u.

questions.prompt: Which vowel is a back unrounded vowel?
questions.explanation: The back unrounded vowels are a and ı; ı is the only such choice.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct locative: sınıf + -DA → ___.
questions.explanation: After voiceless f, -DA becomes -ta; the final vowel ı is back.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct locative: ağaç + -DA → ___.
questions.explanation: After voiceless ç, -DA becomes -ta; the final vowel a is back.

questions.prompt: Complete with the accusative: ağaç + -(y)I → ___.
questions.explanation: Ağaç softens final ç to c before accusative -ı: ağacı.

questions.prompt: Complete with the accusative: renk + -(y)I → ___.
questions.explanation: Renk takes the accusative as rengi, with final k → g.

questions.prompt: Complete: anne + third-person singular possessive → ___. (his/her mother)
questions.explanation: After vowel-final anne, third-person possessive uses buffer s: annesi.

questions.prompt: Complete: oda + third-person singular possessive → ___. (his/her room)
questions.explanation: Oda takes the third-person possessive suffix with buffer s: odası.

questions.prompt: Choose the neutral, non-emphatic subject–object–verb (SOV) order for “Zeynep is drinking tea.”
questions.explanation: The neutral order is subject Zeynep, object çay, verb içiyor; alternatives may be possible in marked contexts.

questions.prompt: Choose the neutral, non-emphatic subject–object–verb (SOV) order for “We are watching a film.”
questions.explanation: Neutral subject–object–verb order is Biz film izliyoruz; other orders can occur for discourse emphasis.

questions.prompt: Which is the standard Turkish written date for “5 November 2026”?
questions.explanation: In the standard written format, the day comes before the month: 5 Kasım 2026.

questions.prompt: Choose the written date meaning “1 January 2027.”
questions.explanation: Ocak means January; Turkish dates commonly place the day first.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative nominal predicate: Biz hazır ___. (We are not ready.)
questions.explanation: Biz hazır değiliz is the first-person plural negative nominal predicate.

questions.prompt: Complete: O öğrenci ___. (He/she is not a student.)
questions.explanation: The third-person singular negative nominal predicate is değil without a personal ending.

questions.prompt: Choose the present progressive: Ben şimdi seni ___. (I am waiting for you now.)
questions.explanation: Beklemek forms the present progressive as bekliyorum, with e → i before -yor.

questions.prompt: Complete the present progressive: Biz şu anda yemeğe ___. (We are starting the meal now.)
questions.explanation: Başlamak forms başlıyoruz in the first-person plural present progressive; the stem-final a narrows to ı.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kitab___ bakıyorum. (I am looking at the book.)
questions.explanation: The dative of kitap is kitaba: p softens to b before the vowel-initial -a. The prompt already supplies kitab-.

questions.prompt: Complete: Dolab___ koyuyorum. (I am putting it in the cupboard.)
questions.explanation: Dolap becomes dolaba with p → b before dative -a; dolaba koyuyorum means I am putting it into the cupboard.

questions.prompt: Complete: İstanbul’___ geliyorum. (I am coming from Istanbul.)
questions.explanation: İstanbul’dan uses -dan because the last vowel u is back and final l is voiced.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ev___ çıkıyorum. (I am leaving the house.)
questions.explanation: Evden uses ablative -den after a front vowel and a voiced consonant.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ders___ sonra eve gideceğim. (After class I will go home.)
questions.explanation: Dersten sonra uses ablative -ten following voiceless s.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “after the meeting”?
questions.explanation: Toplantıdan sonra uses the ablative -dan before sonra.

questions.prompt: Which means “Mehmet’s car”?
questions.explanation: Mehmet’in marks the possessor with genitive; arabası has third-person possessive -sı.

questions.prompt: Which means “the child’s room”?
questions.explanation: Çocuğun odası has genitive çocuğun and possessive odası; çocuk softens to çocuğ-.

questions.prompt: Which is an adjective + noun phrase meaning “a quiet street”?
questions.explanation: Sessiz is an adjective modifying the noun sokak; the other phrases are noun compounds.

questions.prompt: Choose the adjective + noun phrase meaning “an old house.”
questions.explanation: Eski modifies ev as an adjective; the other choices are noun constructions.

questions.prompt: Complete the past progressive: Ben dün saat dokuzda kitap ___. (I was reading a book at nine yesterday.)
questions.explanation: Okuyordum is first-person singular past progressive.

questions.prompt: Complete: Onlar dün akşam televizyon ___. (They were watching TV last night.)
questions.explanation: İzliyorlardı expresses third-person plural past progressive.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning “coffee and tea.”
questions.explanation: İle can coordinate nouns, meaning and, as in kahve ile çay.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “I went with Ayşe”?
questions.explanation: Ayşe ile gittim means “I went with Ayşe.” İle marks accompaniment; Ayşe için means “for Ayşe,” and Ayşe’ye indicates movement toward Ayşe.

questions.prompt: Complete the locative relative: Masa___ kitap benim. (The book on the table is mine.)
questions.explanation: Masadaki modifies kitap: masa + da + ki.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “the person at home”?
questions.explanation: Evdeki is the locative relative adjective modifying kişi.

questions.prompt: Choose the future-in-the-past form: Biz gelecektik ama hastalandık. What does gelecektik mean?
questions.explanation: Gelecektik expresses a past plan or expectation to come.

questions.prompt: Complete the past intention: O arayacak___ ama unuttu. (He/she was going to call, but forgot.)
questions.explanation: Arayacaktı expresses a past plan or intention: ara-yacak-tı. The future suffix ends in k, which remains k before the consonant-initial past marker -tı.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative future-in-the-past. Fill only the missing portion before -tik: Biz git___tik. (We were not going to go.)
questions.explanation: Gitmeyecektik = git- + -me + -yecek + -tik. Since -tik is already printed after the blank, choose only -meyecek.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “She was not going to buy it”?
questions.explanation: Almayacaktı expresses a negative future intention viewed from the past.

questions.prompt: Complete: ___ göre bu film çok güzel. (In my opinion, this film is very good.)
questions.explanation: Bana göre means in my opinion; göre requires the dative.

questions.prompt: Which expression means “according to the teacher”?
questions.explanation: Öğretmene göre uses the dative ending -e with göre.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu çanta seninki ___ ağır. (This bag is as heavy as yours.)
questions.explanation: Seninki kadar ağır compares equal degree of heaviness.

questions.prompt: Which means “as tall as my brother”?
questions.explanation: Kardeşim kadar uzun expresses equal degree with kadar.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported negative nominal predicate: Meğer onlar evde ___ . (Apparently they were not at home.)
questions.explanation: Değilmişler expresses an inferred or reported negative nominal predicate for onlar.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “Apparently the shop was not open”?
questions.explanation: Değilmiş marks a reported or newly discovered negative nominal predicate.

questions.prompt: Which reported/inferred nominal question means “Was Ali apparently sick?”
questions.explanation: Ali hasta mıymış? uses the separate question particle mı followed by the reported/inferred past form -ymış. The other options ask about a present or directly known past condition, or address “you.”

questions.prompt: Complete the reported nominal question: Bu ev eski ___? (Was this house apparently old?)
questions.explanation: Eski miymiş? asks whether it was reportedly or apparently old.

questions.prompt: Choose the negative reported present progressive: O şimdi çalış___ . (Apparently he/she is not working now.)
questions.explanation: Çalışmıyormuş is çalış- + -mı- + -yor + -muş.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “Apparently they are not coming”?
questions.explanation: Gelmiyorlarmış is the negative reported present progressive.

questions.prompt: Which question uses the reported/inferred form to ask whether he was NOT coming?
questions.explanation: Gelmiyor muymuş? asks whether he apparently was not coming: gel-mi-yor (negative progressive) + muymuş (reported question). Gelmiyor muydu? instead asks directly about the past.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported progressive question: Yağmur yağıyor ___? (Was it apparently raining?)
questions.explanation: Yağıyor muymuş? is the reported present-progressive question; the particle is mu after -yor.

questions.prompt: Which asks “Was she apparently going to leave?” using the reported future?
questions.explanation: Ayrılacak mıymış? uses future -acak and reported question miymiş.

questions.prompt: Complete: Toplantı yarın başlayacak ___? (Was the meeting apparently going to start tomorrow?)
questions.explanation: Başlayacak mıymış? uses mı after the back vowel a in -acak.

questions.prompt: Choose the first-person singular aorist: Ben hafta sonları erken ___. (I get up early on weekends.)
questions.explanation: Kalkarım is the first-person singular aorist of kalkmak.

questions.prompt: Complete the habitual sentence: O her sabah çay ___. (He/she drinks tea every morning.)
questions.explanation: İçer is the third-person singular aorist, appropriate for a repeated habit.

questions.prompt: Choose the ability form: Biz yarın size yardım ___. (We can help you tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: Yardım edebiliriz is first-person plural ability.

questions.prompt: Complete: Biz bu soruyu çözebil___ . (We can solve this question.)
questions.explanation: Çözebiliriz combines ability with first-person plural -iz.

questions.prompt: Complete the past negative habit: Çocukken kahve iç___ . (I did not use to drink coffee as a child.)
questions.explanation: İçmezdim expresses a negative past habit.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “We did not use to go there”?
questions.explanation: Gitmezdik is the first-person plural negative aorist in the past.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported past habit: Dedemin anlattığına göre, eskiden burada kar yağar___ . (According to my grandfather, it apparently used to snow here.)
questions.explanation: Yağarmış combines the aorist -ar with the reported/inferred past -mış. The grandfather’s account supplies the reported-information context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence reports that someone apparently used to walk to school?
questions.explanation: Yürürmüş is the reported aorist, expressing a habit known from a report.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative reported habitual form: Eskiden et yemez___. (Apparently he/she did not use to eat meat.)
questions.explanation: Yemezmiş combines negative habitual -mez with reported past -miş.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “Apparently she never used to smoke”?
questions.explanation: İçmezmiş reports a negative former habit learned indirectly.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning “the window of the teacher’s office”.
questions.explanation: Öğretmenin odasının penceresi has genitive–possessive marking at both links.

questions.prompt: Complete the phrase: okulun bahçe___ kapısı (the gate of the school’s garden).
questions.explanation: Bahçesinin marks the school garden as the possessor of the gate: okulun bahçesinin kapısı.

questions.prompt: Complete the possessive verbal noun agreeing with senin: Senin burada kal___ iyi olur. (It would be good for you to stay here.)
questions.explanation: Kalman is the nominalized verb kal-ma with second-person possessive -n.

questions.prompt: Choose the unmarked (non-accusative) possessive verbal-noun phrase for “your leaving early” (addressing one person). The subject is senin.
questions.explanation: Senin (your) requires second-person singular agreement on the verbal noun: git-me-n → gitmen. Gitmeni has an additional accusative -i and is grammatical in some contexts, but not the unmarked form requested.

questions.prompt: Complete: Doktorla konuşmak ___ hastaneye gittim. (I went to the hospital to speak with the doctor.)
questions.explanation: Konuşmak üzere marks the purpose of the hospital visit: “I went to the hospital in order to speak with the doctor.” The alternatives kadar, sonra, and önce do not form the intended purpose construction here.

questions.prompt: Which expression means “in order to learn Turkish” using -mek üzere?
questions.explanation: Öğrenmek üzere is the infinitive followed by üzere, expressing purpose.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kitabı oku___ sonra uyudum. (After reading the book, I slept.)
questions.explanation: Okuduktan sonra means after reading; oku- takes -duktan.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “We ate after the film ended”?
questions.explanation: Bittikten sonra marks an event completed before the next action.

questions.prompt: Complete: Yemek ye___ önce ellerini yıka. (Wash your hands before eating.)
questions.explanation: Ye- (eat) + -meden + önce yields yemeden önce (“before eating”). The negative converb -mAdAn plus önce expresses “before doing.”

questions.prompt: Which means “before sleeping”?
questions.explanation: Uyumadan önce combines -madan with önce to mean before sleeping.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kapıyı aç___ içeri girdim. (I opened the door and entered.)
questions.explanation: Açıp uses the converb -ıp after the back unrounded vowel a.

questions.prompt: Complete: Eve gel___ yemek yaptım. (I came home and cooked.)
questions.explanation: Gelip takes -ip after the front unrounded vowel e.

questions.prompt: Complete: Hiç konuş___ odadan çıktı. (He/she left the room without speaking.)
questions.explanation: Konuşmadan is konuş- (speak) + -madan (“without speaking”). Hiç reinforces that no speaking took place.

questions.prompt: Which means “without looking”?
questions.explanation: Bakmadan is the negative converb expressing without looking.

questions.prompt: Complete: Çocuk gül___ odaya girdi. (The child entered the room laughing.)
questions.explanation: Gülerek uses -erek after the front vowel ü.

questions.prompt: Which means “walking” as a manner of movement?
questions.explanation: Yürüyerek is the manner converb of yürümek.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatical sentence in which an infinitive functions as the subject and means “Reading is useful.”
questions.explanation: Okumak is an infinitive nominal subject.

questions.prompt: Complete: Her gün yürü___ sağlıklıdır. (Walking every day is healthy.)
questions.explanation: The verb stem yürü- takes the infinitive ending -mek: yürümek (“to walk” or “walking”). In Her gün yürümek sağlıklıdır, the infinitive phrase functions as the subject.

questions.prompt: Complete: Senin konuş___ çok güzel. (Your speaking is very nice.)
questions.explanation: Konuşman is the second-person possessive verbal noun.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “your reading the book” (addressing one person)?
questions.explanation: Senin okuman agrees with the second-person genitive subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the plural ending for şehir (city).
questions.explanation: The last vowel i is front, so şehir takes -ler: şehirler.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct plural of çocuk (child)?
questions.explanation: The last vowel u is back, selecting -lar: çocuklar.

questions.prompt: Which of these Turkish consonants is voiceless (unvoiced)?
questions.explanation: Ş is voiceless; z, v, and m are voiced.

questions.prompt: Which noun takes -ta (rather than -da) in the locative singular?
questions.explanation: Kitap ends in voiceless p, so kitap + -DA → kitapta. Ev, okul, and masa take -de/-da instead (evde, okulda, masada).

questions.prompt: Complete: burun + your (singular) → ___.
questions.explanation: Burun loses its second vowel before the second-person singular possessive: burnun.

questions.prompt: Complete: karın (belly) + my → ___.
questions.explanation: Karın undergoes vowel deletion before the possessive suffix: karnım.

questions.prompt: Complete: ağız + my → ___.
questions.explanation: Ağız loses its second vowel before the first-person possessive ending: ağzım.

questions.prompt: Complete: ağız + dative → ___.
questions.explanation: Before the vowel-initial dative suffix, ağız loses its second vowel: ağza.

questions.prompt: Complete: şu + accusative → ___.
questions.explanation: The demonstrative pronoun şu takes the linking n before the accusative -u: şu + n + u → şunu. Şuna is dative, not accusative.

questions.prompt: Complete: o + ablative → ___.
questions.explanation: The demonstrative o uses pronominal n before the ablative suffix: ondan.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct bare adjective–noun phrase meaning “an old house” (not a complete sentence).
questions.explanation: In a bare adjective–noun phrase, the adjective precedes the noun: eski ev.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct bare adjective–noun phrase meaning “a small garden” (not a complete sentence).
questions.explanation: Küçük modifies the noun bahçe and precedes it.

questions.prompt: In “çok eski kitap”, which word is the head noun?
questions.explanation: Kitap is the head noun; çok eski modifies it.

questions.prompt: In “oldukça büyük bahçe”, which word is the head noun?
questions.explanation: Bahçe is the head noun, modified by oldukça büyük.

questions.prompt: Which expression means “It is half past seven”?
questions.explanation: Saat yedi buçuk means 7:30. Yediye çeyrek var is 6:45; yediyi çeyrek geçiyor is 7:15; sekiz buçuk is 8:30.

questions.prompt: Which expression means “It is half past nine”?
questions.explanation: Saat dokuz buçuk means 9:30.

questions.prompt: Complete the first-person plural suggestion: Akşam film izle___! (Let’s watch a film tonight.)
questions.explanation: İzleyelim is the first-person plural optative of izlemek.

questions.prompt: Which sentence makes the suggestion “Let’s eat together”?
questions.explanation: Yiyelim is the first-person plural optative, used to suggest a joint action.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means “Let’s not wait”?
questions.explanation: Beklemeyelim is the negative first-person plural optative.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative suggestion: Bugün dışarı çık___! (Let’s not go out today.)
questions.explanation: Çıkmayalım is the negative first-person plural optative of çıkmak.

questions.prompt: Which word means “in German” (as a language)?
questions.explanation: Almanca is the language name formed from Alman with -ca.

questions.prompt: Which word means “in English” (as a language)?
questions.explanation: İngilizce is the language name with -ce.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “This bag is as heavy as that bag.”

options.text: Bu çanta o çanta kadar ağır.

questions.explanation: Kadar marks equality of degree: o çanta kadar ağır.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “My brother is as tall as me.”
questions.explanation: Benim kadar uzun expresses equality of height.

questions.prompt: Zeynep is not answering her phone. Which sentence uses the third-person predicate ending -DIr to express a possible supposition about her location?
questions.explanation: Zeynep şimdi evdedir includes -dir, which may suggest “Zeynep is probably at home now” in an appropriate context. It may also be a formal assertion; the ending is not exclusively inferential.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses the third-person predicate ending -DIr to make a present-time statement about cold weather.
questions.explanation: Şimdi hava soğuktur uses -tur, the voiceless-consonant variant of -DIr. It is a present-time predicate and may sound formal or categorical; this item identifies the suffix, not a uniquely inferential meaning.

questions.prompt: Complete the formal third-person predicate: Bu cevap doğru___. (This answer is correct.)
questions.explanation: Doğrudur uses the third-person formal/assertive suffix -dur after the vowel-final adjective doğru.

questions.prompt: Choose the formal third-person statement meaning “The room is clean.”
questions.explanation: Temizdir uses -dir for a formal third-person statement.

questions.prompt: According to what people say, Ali used to swim every summer. Choose the reported-habitual sentence.
questions.explanation: Yüzermiş combines the aorist habitual -er with reported -miş.

questions.prompt: Complete the reported habitual: Duyduğuma göre eskiden burada çalış___ . (Apparently, he/she used to work here.)
questions.explanation: Çalışırmış reports a habitual activity learned from another source.

questions.prompt: Choose “my sister’s room’s window.”
questions.explanation: Kız kardeşimin odasının penceresi nests two genitive–possessive relationships.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “the color of my father’s car”?
questions.explanation: Babamın arabasının rengi marks the nested possessive relationships.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that explicitly says “I am glad YOU came” (not I or someone else).
questions.explanation: Senin gelmene makes the second-person subject of the nominalized action explicit.

questions.prompt: Complete the second-person singular possessive verbal noun: Senin erken kalk___ gerekiyor. (You need to get up early.)
questions.explanation: Senin is the second-person singular genitive subject; kalk-ma-n is the matching possessive verbal noun. The full sentence is Senin erken kalkman gerekiyor.

questions.prompt: The train is about to depart. Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Hareket etmek üzere expresses an imminent departure.

questions.prompt: Complete: Film başla___; hemen yerimize oturalım. (The film is about to start; let’s sit down.)
questions.explanation: Başlamak üzere means the film is about to start.

questions.prompt: Complete: Kahve iç___ önce su içiyorum. (I drink water before drinking coffee.)
questions.explanation: Yemeden önce expresses “before eating.”

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence meaning “Call me before you leave.”
questions.explanation: Gitmeden önce expresses “before leaving.”

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the repeated form güle güle to describe someone leaving cheerfully?
questions.explanation: Güle güle is a repeated form associated with smiling or laughing; here güle güle ayrıldı means the child left cheerfully. The expression is also used independently as a farewell, so this item still needs native-speaker review.

questions.prompt: Complete with the repeated -A converb: Eve ___ geldik. (We came home running continuously.)
questions.explanation: Koşa koşa is the repeated -A converb of koşmak.

questions.prompt: Which expression is the conventional paired -A converb meaning “laughing and playing”?
questions.explanation: Güle oynaya is the conventional paired -A converb. Gülerek oynayarak and gülüp oynayarak use different converb endings; they are not necessarily ungrammatical, but they do not match the requested form.

questions.prompt: Complete using the conventional paired -A converb: Çocuklar ___ eve döndüler. (The children returned home cheerfully, laughing and playing.)
questions.explanation: Güle oynaya is the conventional paired -A form. Other choices use different converb morphology and therefore do not answer this specifically worded question.

questions.prompt: Which option repeats the -A converb of ağlamak to express sustained or repeated crying?
questions.explanation: Ağlaya ağlaya repeats the -A converb of ağlamak. The other options repeat different forms or endings, not the requested -A converb.

questions.prompt: Complete with the reduplicated -A converb: Bebek ___ uyudu. (The baby fell asleep while crying continuously.)
questions.explanation: Ağlaya ağlaya conveys repeated or sustained crying accompanying the process of falling asleep; the converb does not itself mean “after.”

questions.prompt: Choose “I heard that Mehmet arrived.”
questions.explanation: Geldiğini is a factive embedded-clause form with possessive and accusative marking.

questions.prompt: Complete: Ayşe’nin sınavı geç___ biliyorum. (I know that Ayşe passed the exam.)
questions.explanation: Geçtiğini is built from geç- + -DIK (with consonant softening before a vowel) + third-person possessive + accusative, yielding “that Ayşe passed.”

questions.prompt: Choose “My mother told me to study.”
questions.explanation: Çalışmamı is a first-person possessive verbal noun with accusative marking.

questions.prompt: Complete: Müdür bana erken gel___ söyledi. (The manager told me to come early.)
questions.explanation: Gelmemi is the first-person nominalized instruction complement.

questions.prompt: Choose “The coach told us to run.”
questions.explanation: Koşmamızı marks us as the people instructed to run.

questions.prompt: Complete: Öğretmen bize sessiz ol___ söyledi. (The teacher told us to be quiet.)
questions.explanation: Olmamızı is the first-person plural possessive verbal noun with accusative marking.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accusative form of saat (clock/hour).
questions.explanation: Saat takes the accusative -i without changing its final t: saat → saati.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly shows a noun retaining its final consonant before the accusative suffix?
questions.explanation: Saat → saati keeps the final t; the other nouns undergo consonant softening in these forms.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct first-person singular possessive form of fikir (idea).
questions.explanation: Fikir loses its second vowel before the vowel-initial possessive suffix: fikir → fikrim.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu konu hakkında bir ___ var. (I have an opinion about this matter.)
questions.explanation: Fikir loses its second vowel before the first-person possessive suffix: fikir → fikrim. The complete sentence is Bu konu hakkında bir fikrim var.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accusative form of zan (supposition).
questions.explanation: Zan doubles n before the vowel-initial accusative suffix: zan → zannı.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accusative form of sır (secret).
questions.explanation: Sır takes consonant gemination before the accusative suffix: sır → sırrı.

questions.prompt: Complete: Bu benim ___. (This is my secret.)
questions.explanation: Sır doubles its final r before the vowel-initial first-person possessive suffix: sır → sırrım. The complete sentence is Bu benim sırrım.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form meaning “my supposition” (zan).
questions.explanation: Zan becomes zannım with consonant gemination before the first-person possessive suffix.
